result:
**No, logging out does not remove the FCM device token on the server.** `src/` has no logout handler. A case-insensitive search for `logout`, `signOut` and `sign-out` found nothing, and `src/auth/auth.service.ts` never calls an unregister method.

Tokens are removed in two ways today:

1. **Explicit client call.** `DELETE unregister-token/:deviceId` (`src/fcm/fcm.controller.ts:51-65`) calls `fcmService.unregisterDeviceToken` (`src/fcm/fcm.service.ts:127-132`). It soft-deletes the row by setting `isActive: false` and `deletedAt`. It only runs if the app calls this endpoint on logout, and nothing on the server enforces that.
2. **Next registration.** `registerDeviceToken` (`src/fcm/fcm.service.ts:96-103`) soft-deletes all of that user's existing tokens through `unregisterAllDeviceTokens` (`:146-150`) before saving the new one. A token is therefore only cleaned up when the same user registers again.

`removeInvalidTokens` (`src/fcm/fcm.service.ts:283-284`) would hard-delete tokens FCM reports as invalid. A search of the non-test code found no caller, so it is dead code. `src/jobs` has no FCM cleanup either.

If the app doesn't call the unregister endpoint on logout, the token stays active after logout. Pushes can then still reach that device, and `getDeviceTokenByUserId` (used at `src/auth/auth.service.ts:230`, `:273` and `:501`) may still return it. I didn't check whether that getter filters on `isActive`.
